hypotheses.name: Entropy Cosmic Evolution
hypotheses.description: Proposes that entropy significantly influences the evolution of the cosmos, shaping space‑time boundaries and large‑scale structures.

hypotheses.name: Altularity
hypotheses.description: Transition to a state of maximum entropy per unit mass.

hypotheses.name: Regime-dependent breakdown
hypotheses.description: Proposed hypothesis that deviations from LCDM predictions cluster in identifiable cosmic time regimes (L0‑L3).

hypotheses.name: Dissipative Structures
hypotheses.description: Structures that maintain themselves by exchanging matter and energy with their surroundings

hypotheses.name: Thermodynamic Temperature Gradient
hypotheses.description: Proposed explanation for the CMB's existence and behavior.

hypotheses.name: Energy Flow Hypothesis
hypotheses.description: c as an emergent property arising from the interplay of energy gradients, entropy, and universal expansion.

hypotheses.name: Regime-Dependent Breakdown
hypotheses.description: The idea that standard cosmological models work brilliantly in some cases but fail spectacularly in others due to regime structure.

hypotheses.name: Regime‑dependent validity
hypotheses.description: The prediction that a phenomenological fitting model is valid only within specific complexity regimes (FLOW vs LATENT).

hypotheses.name: Energy-Entropy Interrelation
hypotheses.description: Proposes a fundamental interrelationship between energy flow and entropy in cosmic evolution.

hypotheses.name: Thermodynamic Field
hypotheses.description: The idea that the universe can be understood as a living, interconnected system of energy flow.

hypotheses.name: Light-Speed Limit
hypotheses.description: The speed of light as a fundamental boundary in energy flow and space-time dynamics.

hypotheses.name: Domain of Validity Theorem
hypotheses.description: Theorem stating that EFC‑R stops precisely where classical potential physics is expected to stop, mapping empirical boundaries of the model.

hypotheses.name: Structure Emergence
hypotheses.description: The natural outcome of energy flow through entropy gradients that leads to the formation of galaxies and fields.

hypotheses.name: Entropy-Driven Evolution
hypotheses.description: The proposition that entropy increase and gradients are primary drivers of cosmic change.

hypotheses.name: Non-Equilibrium Cosmology
hypotheses.description: The view that the cosmos is fundamentally out of thermodynamic equilibrium, shaping its evolution.
